decisions.summary: One command `make record` (assemble / CHECK=1 / PAGE= / SPLIT=), and the citations page assembled in TWO PASSES so `citations.py` keeps reading an assembled page
decisions.why: Unchanged as a fidelity matter, and the Makefile target landed with all three modes. Round 2's caveat (b) is now recorded - the contract says the works block sits `between the two marker comments the derivation itself emits`, and `with_works()` raises without them. Caveat (a) is NOT recorded anywhere: `citations.derive(page_rel, research_dir)` reads the citations page from DISK and has no in-memory form, so `hand that page to the existing derivation` means the first-pass page must be WRITTEN before the derivation is called. Stage 3 has not landed, so this remains the implementation's to honor; it is not a fidelity departure either way.

decisions.summary: A page is a directory of fragments: _front, NNN-<slug>, _tail, prefixes gapped by ten, three digits a question and four a registry entry
decisions.why: FR-011 and FR-012 state exactly this. Now also verified on disk: `research/ways/` holds 010- to 050- question fragments plus _front and _tail, `research/sources/010-works-cited/` holds 0010- to 9200- four-digit entries gapped by ten, and `research/cities/capitals/` the same shape one level down.

decisions.summary: The citing rules and the re-sourcing queue ride inside _front.html as part of the commented-out block rather than each becoming its own file

The landed splitter enforces it and its test (`a heading inside a comment is not a section`) asserts the registry's three section ids.

The 14 `<h3>` inside questions stayed inside their questions.

decisions.summary: The constitution XIII baseline is a detached-worktree `make done`, recorded as m:baseline-done
decisions.why: RESOLVED. Round 2's leftover is fixed: measurements.json no longer holds `baseline-quick`, and the single entry `baseline-done` names `make done` in /tmp/base258 at origin/main 9d11c6e2, with the reason the first attempt was void (taken at a HEAD carrying this feature's own spec, failed on spec-lint over it). The entry is a declared placeholder - value 0, note `RUNNING at the time of writing` - so it is not yet a measurement; it must carry the run's real result before the regression comparison in T27 can be made against it.

decisions.summary: Stage 3 MOVES the notes on the 16 pages whose references are not ascending; the invariant held is the assertion-to-note PAIRING plus the unchanged multiset of note bodies per page
decisions.why: Unchanged from round 2: entailed by the structure the GM approved (notes split by the SAME section as the prose, siblings of their question) plus the renumbering he brought into scope with `do that as part of it`; declared in the stage table, D4a, the contract's invariant section, spec SC-003, US4 scenario 1 and T17/T18, with an order-aware test.

decisions.summary: Stage 3's works list at the top of a citations page REORDERS with the notes, on the same 16 pages; declared as the third reader-visible change, with the SET of works held and its order required to equal the document order of first citation
decisions.why:
RESOLVED by option (i) of round 2's block, and the premise re-verified in code here: `citations.cited_keys()` walks `page_notes` in page order and appends each key on first sight, so reordering the notes reorders the works list; there is no in-memory path that avoids it while FR-029 keeps `citations.py` reading the assembled page. It is now declared in all three places the block named - plan D4a's `And the works list moves with them`, spec SC-003, and the contract's invariant list - and what the test holds is the SET per page plus the order-equals-document-order-of-first-citation claim, which is checkable. Legitimate because it is entailed by decisions the GM approved (notes beside their question, numbers allocated in document order, one reader of the record) and because his byte-identity bar in approved point 3 is attached to the FIRST landing, which stages 1 and 2 met - re-verified here, 20 pages in sync and an empty diff. ONE CORRECTION OWED, which the ruling does not rest on: the plan's supporting sentence says `the list's own heading says "in order of first citation"`, and that is false as measured - all 19 citations pages carry `

The works cited on this page

` and no order claim; the phrase lives in `citations.py`'s docstring, `interactive/CLAUDE.md` and `research/CLAUDE.md`, which are the derivation's own contract and not anything a reader sees. The honest form of the sentence is that the derivation's documented contract, not the page's heading, is what the reorder makes true.
